reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10010 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". This order created a board of three members to investigate the disputes between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company and other carriers named in List A and employees represented by the sixteen cooperating railway labor organizations named in List B; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in an organization of railway employees or in a carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by November 17, 1948); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred the carriers involved and their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the board's own report (a text of PDF pages 1-8 of 70 from the National Mediation Board site, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) carries the date December 17, 1948 on its title page and states that the parties stipulated on the record to extend the time for the board to submit its report to the President until December 17; thirty days after December 17, 1948 is January 16, 1949. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end. Executive Order 10015, signed November 5, 1948 and published at 13 FR 6601 in the Federal Register of November 9, 1948, amended this order effective as of October 18, 1948, the date its own text states: it adds six named carriers to List A and gives new designations to two organizations named in List B, so that after the amendment List A includes those six carriers and the two organizations carry the new designations. It does not change the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report requirement or the standstill, and it does not revoke or supersede this order; it is therefore a later amendment and not an end, and it is recorded as a later event on this clause. The same table in Executive Order 12553 also lists number 10015 with the subject "Amending an order creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes", so the amending order was revoked on the same date by the same sentence.
